title: Give Up to Get More: Priors, Not Policies, Govern Test-Time Compute Allocation
abstract: arXiv:2611.06372v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When many inputs share a budget of repeated attempts by a large language model (LLM), a common rule gives harder inputs more. On public math, code and formal-proof samples, the best published difficulty-proportional rule captures half or more of the oracle gain on benchmarks the model mostly solves, but at most 13% on hard workloads, even given true pass rates. Because the value of one more attempt peaks at intermediate difficulty, the optimal static allocation is inverted-U and gives little to inputs that are hopeless at the current budget. In a strict survey of 221 LLM allocation papers, at least 13 give the hardest inputs the most attempts; their easier settings sit at budgets where this is near-optimal, so the cost appears on harder workloads. Acting on it requires knowing which inputs are solvable, so information, not the policy, drives the gain. With a verifier and a prior from a related model's past runs on the same inputs, Thomps

translated_title: 放弃以获得更多：主导测试时计算分配的是先验而非策略
translated_abstract: 当多个输入共享大语言模型（LLM）的重复尝试预算时，一种常见的规则是给较难的输入分配更多尝试次数。在公开的数学、代码和形式化证明样本上，已发表的最好难度比例规则在模型大多能解决的基准上可以获得一半或更多的oracle增益，但在困难工作负载上最多只能获得13%的增益，即使给定真实的通过率也是如此。由于多一次尝试的价值在中等难度处达到峰值，最优的静态分配呈倒U形，对在当前预算下几乎无望的输入只分配极少的资源。在一项对221篇LLM计算分配论文的严格调查中，至少有13篇论文给最难的输入分配最多的尝试次数；它们的较简单设置恰好处于这种策略接近最优的预算范围内，因此其代价会在更困难的工作负载上显现。要采取正确行动需要知道哪些输入是可解的，因此是信息而非策略本身驱动了增益。借助验证器以及来自相关模型在相同输入上历史运行记录的先验，Thompson（采样方法）……
tldr: 该研究揭示了测试时计算的最优静态分配呈倒U形——应将尝试次数集中在中等难度而非最难的输入上，并指出真正的收益来源于知道哪些输入可解的先验信息，而非分配策略本身。
en_tdlr: The optimal test-time compute allocation follows an inverted-U shape—concentrating attempts on intermediate-difficulty inputs rather than the hardest ones—and the gains come from priors about which inputs are solvable, not from the allocation policy itself.
